newsitem.title: ITALY: Activist says he shot Italian Tyrolean nationalist.
newsitem.headline: Activist says he shot Italian Tyrolean nationalist.

text.p: A leading German-speaking activist in Italy's Alto Adige region confessed on Friday to killing South Tyrolean nationalist Christian Waldner, police and magistrates said.

Waldner, a councillor of the northern region's government for a party seeking independence from Italy, was shot five times on Monday night in a castle hotel where he lived outside Bolzano, the regional capital.

Police said Peter Paul Rainer, described as a leading figure in a German-speaking cultural group known as the Shuetzen which is organised along paramilitary lines, had confessed to the murder hours after being arrested early on Friday.
Rainer and other leading members of the Freiheitiche, a splinter group of the mainstream German-speaking Sudtiroler Vokspartei party, had been questioned extensively about the murder, police said.
"Rainer furnished a version of the facts, but allow me not to divulge it as it must be looked into further," prosecutor Cuno Tarfusser told a news conference in Bolzano.
"We are now looking into possible motives," Tarfusser said, adding that investigators were considering all angles including a political motive.
Police have said they believed Waldner, 37, was shot in the entrance hall of the hotel with a hunting rifle and his body then carried to his suite.
The Alto Adige bi-lingual region was ceded to Italy by Austria after World War One.
